newsitem.title: INDIA: TEXT-Amendments to Indian exchange control manual.
newsitem.headline: TEXT-Amendments to Indian exchange control manual.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Thursday said the following amendments have been made to the exchange control manual (ECM).
The following is the text of a letter sent by the RBI to all authorised dealers in foreign exchange.
Dealers said the amendments detailed changes already announced in Tuesday's monetary policy announcement.
1. FORWARD COVER BASED ON BUSINESS PROJECTIONS:
In terms of paragraph 3C.2 of ECM, before a forward contract is booked with resident customers, authorised dealers are required to ensure that a firm exposure exists in the underlying transaction.

Having regard to the administrative difficulties experienced by the merchant community in producing evidence of exposure in all cases and limitations on banks in critically verifying the documents, it has since been decided that insofar as it relates to exporters and importers, authorised dealers may book forward contracts on the basis of a declaration of an exposure by the customer, subject to the following conditions.
+ The forward contract booked should in the aggregate not exceed the average of the actual export/import figures of the applicant for the preceding two years.
+ The corporate should furnish a certificate to the effect that the exposures covered by the contract have not been covered with any other authorised dealer.

+ Where applicable, the board of directors of the company should fix the limits for their authorised officer to book/cancel/rebook contracts to manage exchange risk and copy of the board's policy in this regard should be filed with the concerned authorised dealer.

It is observed that several corporates having foreign exchange exposure arising out of overseas borrowing/import commitments and those expecting to receive foreign exchange on account of long term export commitments given the market's constraints are now not in a position to obtain to obtain forward cover for longer terms and have to hedge their risks byrolling over forward cover for shorter term which, besides being inefficient, is expensive.

There are also entities in the system who do not have any forex exposures but are willing to assume a forex liability in respect of a whole or part of their rupee liability. It has been decided to allow authorised dealers to enter into foreign currency-rupee swaps to assist the exchange of liability between the foregoing categories of entities and absorb the residual currency/interest mismatches within the authorised dealers open position/gap limits.

Regarding paragraph 5B.2 of ECM, authorised dealers are required to ensure that the balances in foreign currency accounts held with their correspondents abroad (nostro accounts) are commensurate with normal business needs.
Authorised dealers are also not permitted to avail of loans, overdrafts and other fund-based credit facilities from their branches/correspondents beyond $500,000 for periods exceeding five days.

With a view to enabling greater integration between the domestic and overseas markets and facilitate free flows so smoothen volatility, it has been decided to remove the restriction on the level of maintenance of balance in the nostro accounts and borrowings from overseas branches/correspondents.

Accordingly, authorised dealers would now be free to manage thebalances in their nostro accounts subject to the lmits that may be approved by their managements and to invest surplus in the accounts upto $10.0 million in terms of paragraph 5b.9(i) of ECM. It has also been decided to permit authorised dealers to borrow from their overseas branches/correspondents upto the amount of $10.0 million without any restriction on repayment thereof or on the use of such funds in India.
Other amendments will be issued subsequently, RBI said.
